clue.text: After food we will give a final message

indicators.note: the words for 'we will' come after the word for food in the answer

parts.note: fare is food, as in 'simple fare'
we will contracts to we'll, here written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone promises a parting speech once the meal is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like it belongs to 'After food', but it only says the second piece follows the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying goodbye is a parting message given to someone leaving.

clue.text: In the country female rushed to get to church

parts.note: rushed means ran
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Out in the countryside a woman hurries to reach the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the country' reads like scenery, but 'the country' is the definition and 'In' only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A European nation, so an example of a country.

clue.text: Meal dad gets in break

indicators.note: dad gets into the word for break, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a break is a rest
pa is an informal word for dad

explanation.surface: Father manages to grab some food during a pause.
explanation.definitionFit: A rather formal synonym for a meal or feast.

clue.text: Restored to health, wife faces difficult situation

indicators.note: the wife letter stands facing, so in front of, the difficult situation

parts.note: to be in a hole is to be in a difficult situation

explanation.surface: A wife confronts a tough predicament after her recovery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faces' here means 'is in front of', putting W before HOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-fashioned sense of healed or sound, as in 'made whole'.

clue.text: Have a rest, being terribly idle now

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of idle now are badly disordered

explanation.surface: Advice to take a break because you are dreadfully lazy at the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges IDLE NOW.
explanation.definitionFit: To recline briefly in order to recover energy.

clue.text: Vehicle with black on — soot?

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A car with black marks on it raises the question of soot.
explanation.definitionFit: Soot is mostly the element from burnt fuel, so the chemical name fits.

clue.text: Fourth-rate in subject — but having possibility of improvement

indicators.note: the fourth-rate letter goes inside the word for subject

parts.note: subject to, as in 'amenable to rules'; liable or answerable
D is the fourth grade after A, B and C

explanation.surface: Something second-class in its subject matter can still be improved.
explanation.walkthrough: AMENABLE means 'subject (to)' or 'answerable'; D goes in to give AMEND-ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable of being revised or corrected for the better.

clue.text: Country pub not good, nothing special

parts.note: a bar is a pub
bad means not good
O is the zero shape for nothing

explanation.surface: A national grumble: the local pub is poor and unremarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country pub' reads as one phrase; 'Country' is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caribbean island nation, so an example of a country.

clue.text: One denied love, writer taking the drug

indicators.note: the word One is refused its love letter, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, before losing a letter
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
a pen is a writer

explanation.surface: Someone rejected in love turns to drink or drugs while writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'denied' drops the O (love) from One; 'taking' just joins the writer to the article that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend a potion that banished grief, so a mythical drug of forgetfulness.

clue.text: Plant available from dale shop

indicators.note: the plant can be made from the letters of dale shop when they are reworked

explanation.surface: A plant you can buy at the shop in the valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'available from' signals the letters of DALE SHOP rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A lily-family flower of Greek myth, which grew in the fields of the dead.

clue.text: The Parisian tour? Go wild!

parts.note: le is French for 'the'
a trip is a tour

explanation.surface: A French tour invites everyone to cut loose.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits differently from its pieces: three letters, then three, as the phrase 'let rip'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for acting without restraint, as in 'let it rip'.

clue.text: Pile of poor quality about to be chucked

indicators.note: chucked means thrown out, so the about letter is removed

parts.note: cheap means shoddy, of poor quality
C is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A heap of shoddy stuff about to be thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'soon', but it is C (circa), dropped from CHEAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A mound or stack of things.

clue.text: Food served by fool to monarch, merry old one coming round

indicators.note: the merry old king surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme was a merry old soul
an ass is a fool
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the monarch

explanation.surface: A dish brought out by a jester to the king while the jolly old monarch gathers round.
explanation.walkthrough: Old King Cole is the nursery-rhyme king who was 'a merry old soul'; 'coming round' has him enclose the fool and the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A stew cooked slowly in a lidded dish.

clue.text: Exhaust water supply after day

indicators.note: the water piece comes after the day letter

parts.note: rain supplies water

explanation.surface: Fumes and plumbing problems once the day is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhaust' is a verb here, not the car part.
explanation.definitionFit: To use up or empty out completely.

clue.text: Examination of child's head in school hospital

indicators.note: the child's first letter goes inside the school hospital word

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a boarding-school sick bay

indicators.note: the head of child is its first letter

explanation.surface: A child gets a scan at the school sick bay.
explanation.walkthrough: A SAN (sanatorium) is a British boarding school's sick room.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical scan is an imaging examination.

clue.text: Spy on other half to achieve a sort of victory

parts.note: to check on someone is to watch or spy on them
a mate is a partner, someone's other half

explanation.surface: Watching your spouse to gain the upper hand.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, the winning position that traps the opposing king.

clue.text: Scottish tower very good on top for making music

indicators.note: the very good word is placed on top of, so before, the tower

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means very good
a broch is an Iron Age round tower in Scotland

explanation.surface: A Scottish tower with something good on top serves as a music venue.
explanation.walkthrough: A broch is a prehistoric round stone tower found in Scotland; 'on top' in an across clue means placed in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Classical bagpipe music of the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Plant needs to have 500 laid off, sadly

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

indicators.note: sadly suggests the letters of laid off are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A firm must make 500 workers redundant, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid off' reads as redundancy; 'sadly' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow spring flower grown from a bulb.

clue.text: Corny fellow who is a sham

definitions.meaning: a scarecrow figure stuffed with dried corn stalks
a weak, fake argument or person set up to be knocked down

explanation.definitionFit: Both a scarecrow made of straw and a feeble pretend opponent built to be defeated.

clue.text: Disease carried by a mean beast

indicators.note: the disease is carried inside the a-and-mean pieces

parts.note: near means stingy, mean
TB is tuberculosis

explanation.surface: A stingy animal is spreading an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' is not average here but stingy: NEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for the aardvark, an African animal.

clue.text: Bird that sounds coarse

indicators.note: sounds signals that the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: coarse means rough

explanation.surface: A bird whose call is harsh.
explanation.definitionFit: A wading bird of the sandpiper family, the male with a frilled neck.

clue.text: Duck and swan unrestricted

parts.note: a duck is a score of zero in cricket, the letter O
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: A duck and a swan roam freely.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of nought; a pen is a female swan.
explanation.definitionFit: Free of limits or barriers.

clue.text: Object travelling in space, yellow, disturbed tribe

parts.note: or is gold or yellow in heraldry

indicators.note: disturbed suggests the letters of tribe are stirred up

explanation.surface: A yellow craft in space unsettles a tribe.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold or yellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacecraft that circles a planet or moon.

clue.text: Scholar in a vehicle blocking street

indicators.note: the a-and-vehicle pieces block the street, sitting inside its letters

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: An academic in a van is holding up traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned person of great knowledge.

clue.text: About to take medicine, unknown as solution to disease

parts.note: re means about, concerning
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Someone is about to take medicine as an unknown cure.
explanation.definitionFit: A cure or treatment that puts an illness right.

clue.text: Man, 21

definitions.meaning: the answer to 21 across, meaning candid or unrestricted

explanation.definitionFit: Both a male first name and a word for candid, plain-speaking.

clue.text: Concoct a brief act that goes wrong

indicators.note: goes wrong signals that the letters of a brief act fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Inventing a short performance that ends in disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes wrong' rearranges A BRIEF ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: To make up or invent something, often falsely.

clue.text: Fireplace will do when one doesn't have sun

indicators.note: the one word lacks the sun letter, so it is removed

parts.note: single means one

explanation.surface: A fireplace will suffice when a person is short of sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: SINGLE (one) loses its S (sun).
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a hearth or fire, as in inglenook.

clue.text: Yours truly is taken in by cleric lower in status

indicators.note: the speaker's word goes inside the cleric's title

parts.note: a dean is a senior cleric
yours truly is the speaker, me

explanation.surface: The speaker is fooled by a churchman of lesser rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' suggests being fooled, but it means placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To degrade or debase someone's standing.

clue.text: Good person, relation of dad's, to become idle

parts.note: ST is a saint, a good person
an agnate is a relative on the father's side

explanation.surface: A virtuous relative on father's side turning lazy.
explanation.walkthrough: An AGNATE is a kinsman through the male line.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop moving or developing, like still water.

clue.text: Wait — there's underwear that is to be put out

indicators.note: put out means removed, so the that-is letters go

parts.note: lingerie is women's underwear
IE is id est, that is

explanation.surface: Hang on: there's underwear that needs putting out.
explanation.walkthrough: LINGERIE minus IE (id est, 'that is').
explanation.definitionFit: To stay on or delay leaving.

clue.text: It sounds like an author or like a vicar maybe

indicators.note: sounds like means the author's name is heard, not spelt

parts.note: J. B. Priestley, the English novelist and playwright

explanation.surface: A word that resembles a writer's name or describes a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: J. B. Priestley wrote An Inspector Calls; his name drops an E.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the manner of a clergyman, as a vicar is one.
